source: fault.yaml L1-9, L33-36 (gold failing resource namespace/yard-ops, cluster-scoped; remediation: kubectl label namespace yard-ops pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline --overwrite, no change to the Deployment), L40-49: the Namespace sets enforce restricted while its warn and audit labels and its approved-level annotation say baseline. gold.json remediation_summary: 'Set the namespace's enforce level back to the approved one ... enforce=baseline ...; removing the enforce label entirely is the interim mitigation'. notes.md L14-18, L54-63 (the Deployment is the designed distractor), L65-67 (baseline canonical, removal the interim mitigation, both on the same object). Value PINNED: the approved level, a policy enum; removal is accepted under the webhook case's removal spellings, because notes.md names it as a fix on the same object (not an object deletion, so no <object> path). Removal spellings include JSON merge patch null and kubectl's trailing-dash form (enforce-). privileged is NOT accepted: it unblocks the pod too, but loosens the namespace past the approved level the warn and audit labels and the annotation name, so it is a value miss, reported with its raw string. Paths: the bracket key form is canonical; quoted-bracket spellings normalize to it and every bracket spelling reads as the dotted form (v3.1), which is accepted, as is kubectl jsonpath's escaped-dot form. No whole-labels path: the map has three keys, not one, and 'metadata.labels' would match a row on any object and accept wiping every label (review of PR #11). Known limitations: a JSON-pointer spelling with the ~1 escape (labels/pod-security.kubernetes.io~1enforce) is not decoded by the normalizer and will miss; `baseline` appears in no output any tool serves, so a value hit is a guess or the removal mitigation, never a read.
